subject: Priv GPU topology & egress shaping proposal for BlueNova onboarding
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex@bluenova.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: SRE Ops <sre@bluenova.com>
Date: 2028-03-27T17:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial capacity ask for private GPU pool

Markus,

Thanks again for a great demo this morning. BlueNova is ready to move from the hosted pilot to a private VPC deployment for our inference stack. High-level asks: 1) target steady-state throughput of ~1.2M tokens/min across the fleet with 95th p50 latency goal under 200ms for small chat queries; 2) ability to absorb 3x burst windows for 20 minutes during marketing campaigns; 3) strict egress shaping to cap external bandwidth to avoid cloud egress spikes.

We attached the SLA and a basic QPS trace from our production tests (see bluenova-sla-requirements.pdf). Two immediate questions we have for planning:
- How do you normally map tokens/min targets to a private GPU pool (per GPU throughput assumptions)?
- What are common network topology constraints you see on-prem (ToR oversubscription, NIC limits, MTU issues) and recommended mitigations?

Can your team sketch a sizing + egress shaping proposal this week? Happy to get RackHost in the thread for co-ordinating crossconnects.

Regards,
Alex Chen
Head of ML Ops, BlueNova

Attachment: bluenova-sla-requirements.pdf
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Alex Chen <alex@bluenova.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-28T09:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask for private GPU pool

Alex — thanks for the clear brief and the SLA doc. We've sketched an initial approach and a short checklist below; attaching a working sizing workbook (privgpu-sizing-v1.xlsx) and a simple ToR-level topology (network-topology-toR-20280328.png).

Executive proposal (summary):
- Baseline throughput assumption: 40k–55k tokens/sec per A100-class GPU core for your model mix (mixed 8k & 32k contexts; we used a weighted profile). That maps to ~2.4M–3.3M tokens/min per 60-GPU pod (safe steady-state at 70% utilization).
- Recommended starting footprint: 2 pods of 60 GPUs each (120 GPUs total). This gives nominal steady-state capacity ~4.8M tokens/min at 70% utilization and room for cache-warmed bursts.
- Burst handling: admission slots + burst-credit bucket. Keep permanent admission for 70% baseline; allow transient credit to absorb 3x bursts for up to 20 minutes using pre-allocated warm pools and KV-cache pinning.
- Egress shaping: implement per-tenant egress policing at the ToR (ingress/egress policers) plus per-flow token-bucket at the host NIC for fine-grained control. Target headroom: cap externally-visible egress to 10Gbps per pod, with graceful degradation (drop to lower-quality quantized model variant first).

Network considerations & mitigations:
- ToR oversubscription: avoid >3:1 aggregation for inference traffic; prefer 1.5:1 in burst-prone racks.
- NIC: prefer 100Gbps uplinks for each 60-GPU pod; enable multi-path and flow pinning to avoid hairpinning.
- MTU: set jumbo frames 9000 where possible to reduce CPU overhead for KV-cache transfers; validate with your switch firmware.
- Crossconnects: pre-stage BGP + prevent hairpinning between storage and compute by colocating model cache hosts in the same leaf.

Operational constraints:
- Cache warmup: plan a 10–15 minute pre-warm window for model prefix caches after any restart or model swap.
- Observability: token-level tracing, per-NIC egress counters, and per-pod prefix-cache hit metrics required for capacity gating.

Next steps: Laura and Karthik will validate the numbers and network assumptions; can RackHost join a quick call tomorrow at 10am PT to confirm crossconnect options? If that works we'll lock the sizing workbook.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Director, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference

Attachments: privgpu-sizing-v1.xlsx, network-topology-toR-20280328.png
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Date: 2028-03-28T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask for private GPU pool

Looping in quick capacity sanity checks and a couple of alternate knobs.

Karthik and I ran the workbook with two alternate assumptions: conservative per-GPU throughput = 38k tokens/sec, optimistic = 52k tokens/sec (both assume mixed prompt/long-context traffic). Key callouts:
- With conservative numbers, 120 GPUs gives ~2.7M tokens/min steady-state at 70% util — still above your 1.2M tokens/min target with comfortable buffer for cache misses.
- Network egress: If you must keep external egress <= 5Gbps per pod, we recommend an additional on-pod model shard cache (small NVMe-backed cache hosts) to reduce external model fetches during bursts. That reduces egress by ~30% in our sim.

Operational suggestions:
- Admission control tiering: Platinum (guaranteed slots), Gold (best-effort with burst credits), Bronze (spill to hosted). This lets us enforce SLA-critical paths while protecting the fleet.
- Fallback: keep an automatic routing plan to Redwood-hosted edge for Bronze traffic when local queue depth exceeds threshold. Document the failover RTO (we typically target <120s).

We can present a 30-minute run-through with BlueNova and RackHost tomorrow 10am PT. Markus: I'll bring the link to the sizing workbook and a short runbook for cache-warmup.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Sr. Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
